description: Multi-dimensional adversarial review of a diff or capability: correctness, security, and spec compliance, with every finding adversarially verified before it is reported.

args.focus: Check against the change's spec delta (openspec/changes/implement-platform-foundation-api/specs/platform-foundation/spec.md) and the store specs admin-access ('Database not published') and content-authoring (CA-D21). Pay attention to: tools/stack.mjs --check-bind accepting anything outside loopback/RFC 1918 (IPv6 forms, IPv4-mapped, leading zeros, hostnames, 0.0.0.0 spellings); compose.yaml ports that bypass DOUCKO_BIND_ADDRESS; backup/restore writing inside a repository, leaking the DB password on the command line or in logs, or restore destroying data without a guard; any path where request body, query or headers reach logs (filters, actuator httpexchanges, Spring debug settings); the security config leaving /api/admin/** or actuator endpoints open; undeclared paths returning anything other than problem+json without driver internals; FixtureProvenanceTest missing fixture roots; the Dockerfile and .dockerignore copying .env or secrets; the .editorconfig ktlint package-name rule disabled.

findings.title: stack.mjs `up` checks the --env-file it was given but starts compose without it
findings.evidence: `parseArgs` accepts `--env-file` for every command, and `refuseConfig()` checks `publishedPortProblems(opts["env-file"])`. But `docker("up", "-d", "--build", "--wait")` builds its argv from `composeArgs()` alone, without `--env-file`. So `node tools/stack.mjs up --env-file safe.env` checks safe.env and then starts the stack with the default `.env`, which may contain `DOUCKO_BIND_ADDRESS=0.0.0.0`. The spec says the launcher SHALL check the bindings compose actually renders, and here it can check a different configuration from the one it starts.
findings.suggestion: Pass the same `--env-file` to the `up`/`down`/`ps` invocations (e.g. a shared `envArgs` added inside `docker(...)`), or reject `--env-file` for anything except `--check-config`. Add a BindAddressTest case for this.

findings.title: Spring Boot auto-configures an in-memory user and logs its generated password, and those passwords are committed in the QA report
findings.evidence: The chain declares no UserDetailsService or AuthenticationManager, so UserDetailsServiceAutoConfiguration matches. The committed report shows its startup log line, e.g. `docs/qa/automated-verification-latest.md:485`: `Using generated security password: 044eeeb0-...`, and the same line appears in every run. No formLogin or httpBasic is configured, so the user can't sign in today. Still, a credential is written to the container logs on every start and into a committed file. When admin-access adds a login, this default user could become usable by accident.
findings.suggestion: Disable the default user, e.g. declare an empty `InMemoryUserDetailsManager()` bean or exclude `UserDetailsServiceAutoConfiguration`. Then regenerate the QA report so the committed passwords are gone.

findings.title: Requests the Spring Security firewall rejects get Boot's /error JSON (or whitelabel HTML), not problem+json
findings.evidence: Only the entry point and AccessDeniedHandler write problem+json. StrictHttpFirewall rejects paths such as `/api//x`, `/api/x;jsessionid=1` or encoded `%2F`/`%2e`, and the default `HttpStatusRequestRejectedHandler` handles them with `response.sendError(400)`. The container then forwards to `/error`, where BasicErrorController answers `application/json` `{timestamp,status,error,path}`, or whitelabel HTML when the client accepts HTML. UndeclaredPathTest uses MockMvc, which never does that error dispatch, so this path is untested. The spec asks for problem+json for undeclared paths "whatever the method".
findings.suggestion: Register a `RequestRejectedHandler` bean that writes the same catalog-titled problem+json (400). Also consider an ErrorController/ErrorAttributes override that renders ProblemDetail for container-level errors. Cover both with a real-server test (`@SpringBootTest(webEnvironment = RANDOM_PORT)`).

findings.title: Fixture provenance roots leave gaps, and Flyway migrations are fully exempt, so seed data in SQL bypasses CA-D21
findings.evidence: `ROOTS = listOf("src/test/resources", "src/test/kotlin", "src/main/resources", "fixtures")` does not cover non-Kotlin files under `src/main/kotlin/`, other source sets (`src/test/java`, `src/it/...`), `tools/`, or the repo root. A PDF or JSON committed there is never flagged. Also, `Regex("""src/main/resources/db/migration/V\d+(_\d+)*__\w+\.sql""")` exempts every migration by file name. A `V3__seed_tasks.sql` that inserts workbook text or answer keys would pass. That matches the spec's exemption text but defeats NFR-4's intent.
findings.suggestion: Walk `git ls-files` (or the whole working tree minus `target/`, `node_modules/`, `.git/`) and flag non-source extensions (pdf/png/jpg/json/csv/…) outside the listed roots. Limit the migration exemption to DDL, e.g. fail on `INSERT` into content tables unless the file is listed. Raise the spec gap in the docs store.

findings.title: Restore keeps objects the dump lacks; an older dump over a newer schema leaves Flyway history out of step
findings.evidence: `pg_restore ... --clean --if-exists` drops only the objects listed in the archive. Restoring a dump from before migration Vn into a database already at Vn replaces `flyway_schema_history` with the older rows but keeps the Vn tables. On the next backend start, Flyway re-applies Vn and fails with 'relation already exists', or `ddl-auto: validate` fails, and the backend never becomes healthy. Restore doesn't warn about this.
findings.suggestion: Before restoring, drop and recreate the schema inside the same single transaction (e.g. `DROP SCHEMA public CASCADE; CREATE SCHEMA public` piped ahead of pg_restore), or compare the archive's latest Flyway version with the live one and refuse on a mismatch. Mention stopping the backend during restore in the usage text.

findings.title: Backup directory permissions are only applied when the directory is newly created; on Windows nothing restricts a custom --out
findings.evidence: `mkdirSync(outDir, { recursive: true, mode: 0o700 })` sets the mode only on directories it creates, and the umask still applies. An existing `~/doucko-backups` or `--out` directory with 0755 keeps its permissions. On Windows the comment relies on 'the profile ACL', but `--out D:\\shared` has no such ACL. The spec says the dump is 'readable only by its owner' on Windows as well.
findings.suggestion: After mkdir, `chmodSync(outDir, 0o700)` on POSIX. On Windows, either restrict `--out` to paths under `homedir()` or set an owner-only ACL (`icacls /inheritance:r /grant:r %USERNAME%:F`). Otherwise, correct the spec claim.

findings.title: Backup's 'outside every repository' check doesn't resolve symlinks/junctions
findings.evidence: `resolve(opts.out ...)` normalises the path lexically, and the loop then checks `existsSync(join(dir, ".git"))` up the lexical parents. If `--out` (or `~/doucko-backups` itself) is a symlink or Windows junction into a working tree, the walk never sees that repo's `.git`. The dump, which holds the child's data (NFR-3), then lands inside the repository.
findings.suggestion: Create the directory, then walk from `realpathSync(outDir)` (and check the same for the default dir).

findings.title: restore.mjs throws a raw Node stack trace when the given path is a directory
findings.evidence: The guard is `if (!file || !existsSync(file))`, and `existsSync` is true for directories. `inDb` then calls `openSync(file, "r")`, which throws EISDIR on Windows (on POSIX, reading a directory fd throws EISDIR as well). Nothing catches it, so the operator sees an uncaught exception instead of the usage message. Nothing is changed, but the error handling here is inconsistent with the rest of the script.
findings.suggestion: Use `statSync(file, { throwIfNoEntry: false })?.isFile()` in the guard and print the usage/refusal message otherwise.

findings.title: GET /error (and non-JSON Accept on an undeclared path) bypasses the problem+json contract and returns a raw 500 / Boot error body
findings.evidence: `authorize(anyRequest, permitAll)` leaves Boot's BasicErrorController reachable at `/error`. Any LAN client (or the child's browser) can request `GET /error` directly. No servlet error status attribute is set, so the controller replies HTTP 500 `application/json` `{"status":999,"error":"None",...}`. That breaks the spec delta 'Undeclared paths answer problem+json' (404, catalog title) and the AGENTS.md rule 'No user input may produce a raw 500'. Similarly, `GET /api/child/x` with `Accept: text/html` can't render the ProblemDetail, so it falls through to the whitelabel HTML 404. No stack trace leaks (include-stacktrace: never), so the impact is contract and NFR-9 conformance, not disclosure. UndeclaredPathTest only covers `Accept: */*`-style requests to /api/** and /does-not-exist; it never requests `/error` itself.
findings.suggestion: Answer a direct `/error` request as 404 problem+json, either with a custom ErrorController/ErrorAttributes that emits ProblemDetail with the catalog title, or by having the security chain or a filter refuse direct (non-ERROR-dispatch) requests to `/error`. Add `/error` and an `Accept: text/html` case to UndeclaredPathTest.

findings.title: Fixture provenance exempts every Flyway migration, so workbook content seeded via SQL is never checked
findings.evidence: `Regex("""src/main/resources/db/migration/V\d+(_\d+)*__\w+\.sql""")` exempts any versioned migration wholesale. A later slice could add `V7__seed_tasks.sql` with INSERTs of real workbook task text or answer keys (NFR-4, CA-D21). The provenance test would stay green, because only the filename shape is checked and not whether the file is DDL. The spec delta allows this exemption, so this is a policy gap, not a spec violation. The other roots (src/test/resources, src/test/kotlin non-.kt, src/main/resources, fixtures) are covered and tested, including the unlisted-file, bad-origin, missing-file, path-traversal and malformed-row cases.
findings.suggestion: Narrow the exemption to DDL-only migrations, e.g. by failing on `INSERT`/`COPY` in migrations unless the file is listed in PROVENANCE.md, or require that seed migrations be listed with self-authored provenance. Consider recording this in the spec delta.

findings.title: Checklist coverage: areas reviewed and found clean; dependency audit NOT run
findings.evidence:
Informational, not a vulnerability. Areas found clean:
- Bind check: tools/lib/compose.mjs:33-42 uses an anchored dotted-quad regex with no leading zeros and an octet ≤255 check, then a 127/8 / 10/8 / 172.16/12 / 192.168/16 allow-list. It refuses `0.0.0.0`, `::`, `::1`, `::ffff:…`, hostnames, `127.1`, `010.0.0.5` and whitespace (JS `$` does not match before a trailing newline). The check reads `docker compose config` host_ip, and an empty host_ip is treated as 0.0.0.0. Both published ports (backend 8080, frontend 8081) interpolate `${DOUCKO_BIND_ADDRESS:-127.0.0.1}`, and db publishes nothing. Explicit `-f compose.yaml` stops compose.override.yaml from loading.
- Backup/restore: pg_dump/pg_restore run via `docker compose exec` over the container's local socket, so no password appears on argv or in logs. The backup walks up the tree and refuses any directory containing `.git`; the file is written `wx`/0600. Restore needs `--yes`, checks the archive with `pg_restore --list`, takes a safety backup, then runs `--single-transaction --exit-on-error`.
- Logging: `log-request-details: false`, web/security at INFO, no request-logging filter, httpexchanges not exposed. Actuator exposure is `health` only, with no show-details.
- Security chain: `/api/admin/**` is denyAll for every method and the refusal is 403 problem+json. CSRF applies only to admin; no sessions or CORS elsewhere.
- Secrets: Dockerfile COPY is selective (pom, .mvn, contract/api, src/main), `.dockerignore` and `.gitignore` exclude `.env`/`.env.*`, `.env.example` holds placeholders only, and the DB password is required via `${…:?}`.
- .editorconfig disables ktlint package-name only for `**/adapter/in/**.kt`.
- No child or admin endpoints exist yet, so there is no IDOR, mass-assignment or answer-key DTO surface to review.

Not verified: `npm audit` and the Maven advisory check were not run in this session (shell permission was denied). Spring Boot parent is 4.1.1.
findings.suggestion: Run `npm audit` and a Maven advisory scan (e.g. OWASP dependency-check or `mvn org.owasp:dependency-check-maven:check`) before G-gate sign-off, and record the result under docs/qa/. Until then, treat the dependency item as NOT-EARNED, not clean.

findings.title: Coverage summary
findings.evidence: 15 scenarios in total: 12 in the change delta, plus admin-access 'Database not published' and content-authoring CA-D21 'Every fixture has a self-authored provenance entry' / 'Unlisted fixture fails the check'. Result: 14 implemented, 1 partial (Unknown child path, because GET /error is not covered), 0 missing, 0 contradicted. All named tests pass in docs/qa/automated-verification-latest.md: 41 unit tests and 5 integration tests, BUILD SUCCESS. The store scenario 'Committing a PDF is refused' (pre-commit hook) is enforced by the installed harness and was not re-audited.
findings.suggestion: No action. This entry only records the summary line.

findings.title: GET /error is an undeclared path that probably answers Boot's BasicErrorController JSON instead of 404 problem+json
findings.evidence: Spec: 'A request to a path the contract does not declare SHALL be answered 404 with an application/problem+json body ... whatever the method'. Contract info: 'A path not declared here is answered 404 with a problem+json body'. Code: `authorize(anyRequest, permitAll)`, and the slice adds no ErrorController override or `server.error.path` change, so a direct GET /error reaches Spring Boot's BasicErrorController. That controller returns application/json ({timestamp,status,error,path}) with a non-404 status, not problem+json. UndeclaredPathTest only covers /api/child/does-not-exist, /api/does-not-exist and /does-not-exist, so this path is untested.
findings.suggestion: Add '/error' (and HEAD/OPTIONS/PATCH variants) to UndeclaredPathTest. If it fails, either refuse direct REQUEST dispatches to /error (allow only DispatcherType.ERROR) so they fall through to a 404 problem, or provide an ErrorController that renders problem+json from the catalog.

findings.title: 'readable only by its owner' is not enforced on Windows or for a pre-existing directory, and is untested
findings.evidence: Spec: '`npm run backup` SHALL write a pg_dump ... to a file outside every repository, readable only by its owner ... on Windows as well as on other platforms (NFR-10)'. Code: `mkdirSync(outDir, { recursive: true, mode: 0o700 })` and `openSync(file, "wx", 0o600)`. The comment admits 'on Windows the profile ACL applies', but Node ignores POSIX modes on Windows, so a `--out D:\shared` dump inherits whatever ACL that directory has. On POSIX, `mkdirSync` applies 0o700 only when it creates the directory, so an existing world-readable ~/doucko-backups stays readable. BackupRestoreIT asserts neither file permissions nor the refusal of an output directory inside a git tree.
findings.suggestion: On POSIX, chmod the directory to 0o700 when it already exists. On Windows, either restrict the ACL (for example `icacls /inheritance:r /grant:r %USERNAME%:F`) or amend the spec to say owner-only is guaranteed only under the default profile directory. Add tests for the in-repo refusal and for the file mode on POSIX.

findings.title: Spring Boot logs a generated security password at startup, and it is committed in the QA evidence
findings.evidence: The verification log contains 'Using generated security password: 044eeeb0-…' (also at lines 522 and 2506). SecurityConfiguration defines a SecurityFilterChain but no UserDetailsService, so UserDetailsServiceAutoConfiguration creates an in-memory user and logs its password, both in tests and in the compose stack. No requirement backs this. It conflicts with the spirit of 'no secrets in logs', and the credential is now in a committed file. The password is not currently usable because neither httpBasic nor formLogin is configured.
findings.suggestion: Declare an empty `UserDetailsService` bean (`InMemoryUserDetailsManager()`), or exclude UserDetailsServiceAutoConfiguration until admin-access ships. Then regenerate the evidence file.

findings.title: NFR-3 scope is narrowed in the spec delta compared with the capability plan ('at any level')
findings.evidence: The plan's NFR-3 row reads: 'backend: logging policy (no request bodies, answers, notes or display name at any level)'. The spec delta reads: 'at the log levels the application configures ... raising them is never a supported configuration'. The AtDebug negative control shows a bound body IS logged at org.springframework.web=DEBUG. The implementation follows the spec delta, which departs from the plan without a recorded decision.
findings.suggestion: Amend contract/docs/mvp-capability-plan.md (docs store) to the 'configured levels' wording, or record a decision. Alternatively, mask bound bodies at DEBUG too, for example with a logback turbo filter on the RequestResponseBodyMethodProcessor and AbstractMessageConverterMethodProcessor loggers.

findings.title: A plain `docker compose up` bypasses the bind-address guard
findings.evidence: Spec: 'The stack launcher SHALL refuse a bind address that is not loopback or a canonical RFC 1918 IPv4 address'. compose.yaml publishes `${DOUCKO_BIND_ADDRESS:-127.0.0.1}:8080:8080`, and the header comment admits 'A plain `docker compose up` skips that check'. With `DOUCKO_BIND_ADDRESS=0.0.0.0` in .env, `docker compose up` publishes on every interface. The launcher (tools/lib/compose.mjs bindAddressProblem / publishedPortProblems) is correct: it refuses IPv6, IPv4-mapped, leading-zero, hostname, whitespace and empty host_ip forms.
findings.suggestion: Accept this and say so explicitly in the spec ('the guard applies to npm run stack:up only'), or make compose fail closed. One option is a one-shot `bind-guard` service that validates DOUCKO_BIND_ADDRESS and that backend/frontend `depends_on` with `condition: service_completed_successfully`.

findings.title: Task 2.9 (RED run before implementation) is unrecorded
findings.evidence: tasks.md: '- [ ] 2.9 Run the tests and confirm RED on assertions ... **Open:** no recorded RED run; only the two logging tests were seen failing against a deliberate leak'. AGENTS.md requires: 'Tests are written from the spec and seen RED before implementation'. The checkbox is honestly left open, but tasks 3.x are ticked without RED evidence for ComposeConfigurationTest, BindAddressTest, UndeclaredPathTest, FixtureProvenanceTest or BackupRestoreIT.
findings.suggestion: Record mutation-style RED evidence: revert each artifact (for example publish the db port, accept 0.0.0.0, permitAll on /api/admin/**) and capture the failing test. Alternatively, record an explicit waiver in docs/qa/evidence.

findings.title: Task 4.5 is unticked although docs/current-state.md was updated in this diff
findings.evidence: tasks.md: '- [ ] 4.5 Update `docs/current-state.md`'. The diff changes docs/current-state.md to 'Current phase: Phase 4 / Last completed gate: G3 / Active change: implement-platform-foundation-api (slice 1, in progress)'. The checkbox does not match reality, in the conservative direction. Task 4.3 (review-gate, review-findings.json clean) is also open while commit 24d6c7a claims 'slice 1 backend review-gate findings' were fixed, and no review-findings.json exists in the change folder.
findings.suggestion: Tick 4.5 at the milestone update, or note that a final update is still pending. Add review-findings.json before ticking 4.3.

findings.title: Undeclared-path test does not cover PATCH, HEAD or OPTIONS ('whatever the method')
findings.evidence: Spec: 'answered 404 ... whatever the method'. The test parametrizes only GET plus `["POST", "PUT", "DELETE"]`. ResourceHttpRequestHandler handles OPTIONS and HEAD specially, so those answers are unverified.
findings.suggestion: Add PATCH, HEAD and OPTIONS to the parametrized cases (HEAD has no body, so assert status only).

findings.title: The NFR-3 log-capture test does not exercise a malformed bound body
findings.evidence: Spec: 'No request body ... SHALL appear in the backend's logs at the log levels the application configures ..., including a body an endpoint binds'. The test sends only well-formed JSON. Jackson's HttpMessageNotReadableException messages quote the offending token, and DefaultHandlerExceptionResolver logs resolved exceptions at WARN, so the main leak path at INFO is not covered by any test.
findings.suggestion: Add an AtConfiguredLevels case that posts `{"a": PII-SENTINEL…}` (invalid JSON containing the sentinel) to ECHO and asserts the sentinel is absent from the output.

findings.title: Requests rejected by the firewall or sent to /error return Boot's error JSON instead of problem+json
findings.evidence: Only MVC-handled 404s and the chain's own 403 are problem+json. StrictHttpFirewall rejects paths like `/api//child/x`, `/api/child/%2e%2e/x` and `/api/child/a;b`. Its default HttpStatusRequestRejectedHandler then calls sendError(400), which dispatches to Boot's BasicErrorController. That controller returns application/json `{timestamp,status,error,path}`, not RFC 7807. A direct `GET /error` (a path the contract doesn't declare, allowed by `anyRequest permitAll`) gets the same legacy body. The spec delta requires undeclared paths to answer problem+json titled from the catalog, and UndeclaredPathTest only covers paths MVC resolves.
findings.suggestion: Register a RequestRejectedHandler bean that writes a catalog-titled problem+json (400 or 404), the same way writeForbidden works. Also either replace the /error rendering with a problem+json ErrorController, or deny direct requests to /error. Add `/api//child/x` and `GET /error` cases to UndeclaredPathTest.

findings.title: Restore with --clean leaves objects that are newer than the dump (Flyway history ends up out of sync)
findings.evidence: `pg_restore --clean --if-exists` only drops objects that are in the archive. If the backup predates a migration, the restore puts back the older flyway_schema_history but keeps the tables and columns the newer migration created. On the next start, Flyway re-applies that migration against objects that already exist and fails. Alternatively Hibernate `validate` fails. Either way the backend won't start after a successful restore, even though the restore reported success.
findings.suggestion: Inside the same single transaction, drop and recreate the `public` schema before restoring, for example with a preliminary `psql -c 'DROP SCHEMA public CASCADE; CREATE SCHEMA public'` run as part of one transaction script. Otherwise, compare the archive's flyway_schema_history max version with the live one and refuse with a clear message. Extend BackupRestoreIT with a table created after the dump was taken.

findings.title: Nested .env files are not excluded from the Docker build context and could be copied into the image
findings.evidence: .dockerignore lists `.env` and `.env.*`. Those patterns only match at the context root. The Dockerfile does `COPY src/main src/main` and `COPY contract/api contract/api`, so a stray `src/main/resources/.env` (or similar under contract/api) would go into the build stage and from there into the jar's classpath resources.
findings.suggestion: Add `**/.env` and `**/.env.*` (keeping `!.env.example` if needed), plus `**/*.dump` and `fixtures/`, so secrets and backups never enter the build context.

findings.title: Backup's in-repository check uses the unresolved path, and the directory mode is only applied on creation
findings.evidence: The `.git` walk runs on `resolve(outDir)`, not on its real path. A junction or symlink such as `~/doucko-backups -> C:/projects/school-tutor/backend/backups` passes the check while the dump lands inside the working tree. `mkdirSync(outDir, { recursive: true, mode: 0o700 })` doesn't change the mode of a directory that already exists, so on POSIX a pre-existing world-readable directory stays that way. The spec requires the dump to be readable only by its owner; the file itself is 0600, but its directory listing isn't protected.
findings.suggestion: After mkdir, run the `.git` walk on `realpathSync(outDir)`. On POSIX, `chmodSync(outDir, 0o700)`, or warn when the existing directory's mode is wider.

findings.title: Fixture roots are hard-coded, so new source sets and non-Kotlin files under src/main/kotlin are never checked
findings.evidence: ROOTS = src/test/resources, src/test/kotlin, src/main/resources, fixtures. A data file committed under `src/main/kotlin/...` (e.g. a JSON answer key beside a use case), or a future `src/integrationTest/resources` or `src/testFixtures/resources`, isn't walked, so it passes silently. The broad exemption `application(-[\w-]+)?\.ya?ml` also lets something like `application-seed.yaml` carry workbook content unchecked.
findings.suggestion: Walk all of `src/` and exempt only `*.kt`/`*.kts` sources, the named config, the message catalog and Flyway files. Narrow the application-config exemption to the profiles that actually exist (`application.yaml` plus an explicit list).

findings.title: The ktlint package-name exemption covers every file under adapter/in, not just the backticked segment
findings.evidence: `[**/adapter/in/**.kt] ktlint_standard_package-name = disabled` turns off the whole rule for every inbound-adapter file. A misnamed package there (uppercase, underscores, a typo) would no longer be flagged.
findings.suggestion: Accept this as a deliberate scoped waiver, but record it in an ADR or in current-state.md. Alternatively, add a small test asserting that files under adapter/in declare `package cz.doucko.<module>.adapter.`in`.web` and match their directory, so the protection the rule gave isn't lost.

result.reasoning:
Confirmed in the code. In tools/stack.mjs:17, `--env-file` is parsed as a value flag for every invocation. `refuseConfig()` (line 27) then calls `publishedPortProblems(opts["env-file"])`. In tools/lib/compose.mjs:51, that function adds `--env-file <file>` to `docker compose config`. On the `up` path (line 39), the guard runs against that file. The start command at line 46 is `docker("up", "-d", "--build", "--wait")`, and the `docker` helper (line 34) builds its argv from `composeArgs()` alone. `composeArgs` (compose.mjs:12-14) returns only `compose -f compose.yaml [-p project]`, so `--env-file` is never passed. That means `node tools/stack.mjs up --env-file safe.env` checks safe.env and then starts compose with the default .env. If that .env sets `DOUCKO_BIND_ADDRESS=0.0.0.0`, the stack publishes on all interfaces, which bypasses the NFR-2 guard. Nothing else forwards the flag or rejects it for `up`.

There is a second, smaller mismatch. The config check runs with `cwd: ROOT`, but `docker()` inherits the caller's cwd. With `-f` this usually resolves .env the same way, but it is still a difference between the two calls.

I'm suggesting a downgrade from major. The usage text (line 52) and the header comment list `--env-file` only for `--check-config`, and `npm run stack:up` does not pass it. To hit the bug, someone has to add an undocumented flag to `up` by hand. The mechanism is real and could defeat a security guard, but only through usage the tool doesn't advertise.

I confirmed the mechanism in the code. In tools/stack.mjs:17, `parseArgs(..., ["check-bind", "env-file"])` accepts `--env-file` for every command. For `up`, line 39 calls `refuseConfig()`, which passes `opts["env-file"]` to `publishedPortProblems`. That function (tools/lib/compose.mjs:51) adds `--env-file <file>` to `docker compose config`. The actual start goes through `docker` (stack.mjs:34), which builds argv from `composeArgs()` only, so `--env-file` is dropped. Compose then falls back to the default `.env` in the project directory, plus the process environment. As a result, `node tools/stack.mjs up --env-file safe.env` checks safe.env, prints "every published port binds an allowed address", and starts with `.env`. If `.env` has `DOUCKO_BIND_ADDRESS=0.0.0.0`, that breaks the NFR-2 guarantee. Nothing else rejects or forwards the flag, and BindAddressTest only covers `--check-bind` and `--check-config --env-file`.

Why I'm downgrading it: an operator has to trigger it, and only with a flag combination the tool doesn't document. The `npm run stack:up` script (package.json:23) passes no `--env-file`, so the documented path checks and starts the same config. The usage text (stack.mjs:7 and :52) only shows `--env-file` with `--check-config`. No remote attacker can reach this, and the person running it controls both files. Still, the tool silently accepts the flag and prints a false safety confirmation, so this is a real correctness bug that defeats the guard. That makes it minor rather than major.

The finding holds up. SecurityConfiguration.kt (lines 32–53) defines only a SecurityFilterChain bean. It does not declare a UserDetailsService, AuthenticationManager, AuthenticationProvider or JwtDecoder. I searched the repo outside target/ and found no other such bean and no autoconfig exclusion. The committed QA report confirms this. docs/qa/automated-verification-latest.md:3990-3994 shows `UserDetailsServiceAutoConfiguration matched` and `@ConditionalOnMissingBean ... did not find any beans`. Lines 485, 522, 2506, 6598 and 6700 each contain `Using generated security password: <uuid>`, and lines 489 and others show the global AuthenticationManager being wired to inMemoryUserDetailsManager. The finding is also right that no formLogin or httpBasic is configured, so nobody can use the user today. Since it already says that, severity minor is right. In openspec/changes/implement-platform-foundation-api/specs/platform-foundation/spec.md:69, the "Unknown child path" scenario names exactly `GET /api/child/does-not-exist`, or a `POST`, `PUT` or `DELETE` to an undeclared path. Through the correctness lens, the finding shows no wrong behaviour. It only says some methods are "unverified". Its stated mechanism also doesn't hold. In Spring 6.1+/7, ResourceHttpRequestHandler.handleRequest looks up the resource first. When there is none, it throws NoResourceFoundException before it reaches its special OPTIONS branch (setting the Allow header). HEAD is handled the same way as GET. So for an undeclared path, OPTIONS and HEAD still go down the same NoResourceFoundException → 404 problem+json path as the methods already tested. There is no custom code in src/main that would make them behave differently (shared/ contains only SharedModule.kt and SecurityConfiguration.kt).

- **Method order in the resource handler.** In Spring 6/7, `ResourceHttpRequestHandler.handleRequest` first calls `getResource()`. When the resource is missing it throws `NoResourceFoundException` (404) straight away. Only after that does it handle OPTIONS (sets the `Allow` header) or check which methods are allowed (would give 405). So the special handling of OPTIONS and HEAD that the finding points to only applies to resources that exist. An undeclared path goes to the same `NoResourceFoundException`, and so to the same 404 problem+json, whatever the method. The existing POST, PUT and DELETE cases show this ordering: if the method check ran first they would return 405, not the 404 the test expects.
- **PATCH.** `SecurityConfiguration` requires a CSRF token only when the default CSRF matcher matches (which includes PATCH) AND the path is under `/api/admin/**`. A PATCH to a non-admin undeclared path therefore behaves exactly like PUT or POST, which the test already covers.

- **OPTIONS.** A CORS preflight (OPTIONS with an `Origin` header) is a separate concern from an undeclared-path request and is not what the finding describes.
